reviews.review_text:
Sonali W
2 contributions
0
Staff ripped me off then insulted me
Nov 2019 • Family
This review is to serve as a warning to other visitors and to bring this to the attention of the restaurant management. I was at the restaurant just a couple of hours ago as part of a full day Ho Chi Minh City tour with TNK travels. We were there for lunch. The restaurant looks lovely with lots of greenery and a pool in the middle. The food was alright and service was quick, however, it was at the end of service that the problem happened. Drinks were not included in our tour package so we ordered them separately, mum and I ordered a passion fruit juice and a lime juice. I paid the bill and noticed that I was short of some change when the staff returned with my change. When I asked him about it, he said something on his language to another staff member who pulled some change out of her own wallet and gave it to me. It was a little more than what I was owed but before I could say anything, the first staff member, Tony, turned to me and said ‘ you can keep the extra as a tip’. Which was obviously an insult. First of all, some of you may already know that Vietnamese currency is complicated, they have no coins, only notes and they even have notes for 500,000 Dong. So when I was short changed, while I really didn’t care whether a paltry 800 dong was given to me or not, I was more curious about whether they actually even have notes for small amounts like that. I wanted to leave a tip for the staff and I assumed I was short changed by mistake. But Tony’s response to a simple inquiry left me very unhappy. You cannot choose to rip off customers and then insult them when you get caught. And then I found out that an older couple from South Africa were also ripped off the same way. So this was a pattern. 

Anyway, I didn’t want to keep the change so I gave it back to them but they kept pushing the note towards me and insisted I keep it. No apology for the mistake or Tony’s little quip. I complained to the tour guide in front of the staff member and told her exactly what happened. Tony and the other staff member kept defending what they did initially. After much discussion, and after I demanded an apology, he said he was sorry. 

I think most Vietnamese people are very pleasant but this was not a good experience. I understand this this restaurant has won awards etc but this was completely undeserving of that sort of recognition. The staff need to be trained to treat all customers regardless of their ethnicity the same way. I didn’t see Tony commenting on the white South African man who was also ripped off and who also demanded his change.
